beats.narration_text: Hej. This is Liam, in for Bear. Claude's desk buddy isn't a product feature. It's an opt-in API for makers, so the real question is how you build one.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. B L E, Bluetooth Low Energy: a low-power wireless link. A permission prompt: Claude asking before it runs a tool. And a reference repo: one worked example, made to be copied.

beats.narration_text: Here's the desk. A laptop runs the Claude app, on Mac or Windows. Beside it sits a tiny device with a screen and buttons. The app can connect your Cowork and Claude Code sessions to it, over Bluetooth.

beats.narration_text: That bridge is off by default, and you opt in. Turn on developer mode, open Hardware Buddy, click connect, and pick your device. After that, it reconnects by itself. It's for makers, not an official product feature.

beats.narration_text: Now the app sends a snapshot whenever something changes, and every ten seconds anyway: how many sessions are running or waiting, plus a few recent transcript lines, newest first. The tiny screen scrolls them.

beats.narration_text: The team's own example is a desk pet, on an E S P thirty-two board. It sleeps when nothing's happening. Start a session, and it wakes up.

beats.narration_text: Now Claude wants to run a Bash command, and it needs your permission. The snapshot carries a prompt: the tool, a short hint, and an ID. It shows up on the device too, and the pet gets impatient. Its light blinks.

beats.narration_text: Press the front button, and the device sends back one line: that same ID, and the decision, once. Once approves that one tool call. The other button sends deny. Approve quickly, and the pet shows hearts.

beats.narration_text: That link carries transcript snippets and tool hints, and an unencrypted one can be read by anyone in radio range with a cheap dongle. So the reference says to require encrypted pairing. The device shows a six-digit pass key, you type it into the app, and the link is encrypted from then on.

shot.visual_intent: Packets ride the arc; a small grey dongle slides in below and a dashed line reaches up to the arc; a six-digit passkey appears on the device screen, then the same digits in the Claude window; a padlock closes on the arc and the dongle's line snaps back.

beats.narration_text: And you don't need any of this code. REFERENCE dot md is the contract: advertise the Nordic UART Service, a standard way to send text over Bluetooth, then trade one line of JSON at a time. An Arduino, or a Raspberry Pi with a Bluetooth dongle, will do. The repo's own advice: the best contribution is a fork.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Here is REFERENCE dot md from Anthropic's claude desktop buddy repo: paste it. Help me plan a tiny device of my own that speaks this protocol: name your device. List what its screen shows from each snapshot, which permission prompts it may approve with a button press, and what it must never do without a person. Plan only; no firmware yet. Then check two things yourself. Find every approval in the plan. Is each one a button press? And open REFERENCE dot md. Do the plan's field names match it exactly?
